Subject: Draft for Denise’s review — Cascade Legal Rights Project response

On behalf of Cascade Legal Rights Project, thank you for raising these concerns. Receiving a letter from a landlord’s law firm shortly after asking for help can be frightening. We understand why that timing would leave people worried about where their information went. People should be able to seek help without fearing that doing so will put them at greater risk.

Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or otherwise disclosing clinic attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Clinic sign-in records are retained internally and kept in locked storage.

Magistrate-court eviction filings are public records, and some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for the letters described here, but we cannot establish the source of a particular mailing from this thread. To protect people’s privacy, we will not confirm whether anyone attended a clinic or discuss any individual’s circumstances here.

We welcome questions about our information-handling policy. Please contact us directly at clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. You do not need to identify yourself as a client or share personal details on this board to raise a concern. Please avoid posting anyone’s name, address, case number, or other identifying information.

The free, walk-in tenant rights clinic is still happening Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Because the library meeting room is closed for repairs, the clinic has moved to Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The accessible side entrance is by the parking lot. No appointment is needed.

Volunteer attorneys and staff will be available to review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options. You are still welcome, including if you have questions or concerns about the clinic. Thank you for giving us the opportunity to respond.

Cascade Legal Rights Project
